# kiss-ssg

> A small, dependency-driven static site generator for Node, built to be driven by a coding agent. MVC-style: Handlebars views, JSON/HTTP/function models, JS controllers. ESM (Node ≥22.12), no build step, no bundler.

This file is the index: what exists, the shape to follow, and the traps nothing reports. Every rule's full statement is in [GUIDE.md](GUIDE.md) (`node_modules/kiss-ssg/GUIDE.md`), under the heading each line below names. Read the section before relying on a behaviour this file only names.

Install: `npm install kiss-ssg --save-dev`; `import Kiss from 'kiss-ssg'`. One `Kiss` instance per build folder, built with `new Kiss(config)` and driven by a chainable API. `.page()`/`.pages()`/`.scan()` queue pages; `.generate()` renders and writes them; `await kiss.complete()` is the verdict.

**Skills.** Two plugins carry the recipes, from this repo's marketplace, not npm. `kiss-ssg` has the task skills `kiss-site-new`, `kiss-site-import`, `kiss-page-add`, `kiss-build-check`, `kiss-site-review`, `kiss-site-migrate`, calling the domain skills `kiss-writing-for-the-web`, `kiss-information-architecture`, `kiss-seo`, `kiss-accessibility`, `kiss-front-end`, `kiss-performance`, `kiss-design`, `kiss-legal-and-privacy`; `kiss-memory` has `kiss-site-brief` and the branch rituals. `npx kiss-ssg init` declares both and prints the install commands for Claude Code and Codex; a declaration alone installs nothing. Offer them to the site's owner before building without them.

## The build script

Name it `router.js` at the project root, with `"type": "module"`, `main` pointing at it, and `build`/`dev`/`check`/`aikb` scripts (`"check": "kiss-ssg check router.js"`, `"aikb": "kiss-ssg aikb router.js"`). It is a router: `new Kiss(config)`, the `.page()`/`.pages()`/`.scan()` table, the `.generate()`/`.sitemap()`/`.llms()`/`.feed()`/`.robots()` chain, and `await kiss.complete().catch(reportBuildFailure)`. Anything else goes in a module beside it. Each extraction has one yes/no trigger, independent of the others (GUIDE.md § The build script):

- **Tier 0, one file:** no custom helpers, no fact stated twice. File length is never a trigger.
- **Tier 1, `helpers/`:** at the **first** custom helper. Its `index.js` exports `registerHelpers(kiss)` and **kiss calls it** from `config.folders.helpers` (default `./helpers`): never register it in the router. Export the pure function; register a thin adapter over it.
- **Tier 2, `config/`:** when one fact (a phone number, an address) appears both in visible markup and in JSON-LD or feed metadata, spread it into `new Kiss()` as a config key. A `complete()` callback that reads `this` stays a `function`, not an arrow.

Keep build-script modules out of `src`: a module in an unrecognised folder under `src` makes every save a rebuild that cannot pick the edit up. Helpers are registered once per process, so read data at render time, not at registration. Renaming a build script breaks Tailwind `@source` globs, `package.json` and CI silently: grep for the old name.

## Building a site well

- **Never hand-write an internal URL.** `{{link "about"}}` for a page and `{{asset "css/site.css"}}` for a file both fail the build when wrong (in dev they warn and carry on). The exceptions: a build opened off the file system (`{{root}}` plus a relative path, `examples/11-blog`), and a file another method writes (`/feed.xml`, `/sitemap.xml`), which has no `{{link}}` — write its path; the link scan still checks it.
- **Content that repeats is data:** one JSON model and one partial, not N copies.
- **Never invent a fact about the business:** mark what is missing.
- **`npx kiss-ssg check <script> --summary` is the bar, and the bar is zero broken links.**
- **Record the knowledge base when work closes** (`npx kiss-ssg aikb <script>`), commit it, and write `AIKB/site.md`'s retired-feedback entries while you remember why.

## API

GUIDE.md § .page(), § .pages(), § Controller, § Waiting for the build, § Other methods.

- `.page(options)`: one page. `view` (`.hbs` under `folders.pages`, or a template string), `model` (`.json` file, models folder → array, `http(s)://` URL, or object), `controller` (function or `.js` file; return new values, never mutate), `title`, `description`, `path`, `slug`, `ext`, `id` (default: the view's route minus `.hbs`, so `menu/index.hbs` is `menu/index`, not `menu`), `aliases` (old paths → 301s), `canonical` (an absolute URL elsewhere: leaves sitemap, `llms.txt` and feed), `generate: false`, `config` (per-page overrides, such as `extensionLess: false` for a literal `404.html`), and the per-output options `ignoreSitemap`/`ignoreLlms`/`ignoreFeed`, `sitemapLastmod` and `package`, each in its output's GUIDE.md section.
- `.pages(options)`: the same, fanned out over an array model; one bad item fails only its own page. An item's id is the registration's route (or `id` as a prefix) plus its slug; a record may carry its own `id` and `aliases`.
- `.scan()`: `.page()` for every unregistered `.hbs` under `folders.pages`.
- `.generate(callback)`: render and write every queued page once. HTML is minified (inline JS/CSS too) except under `dev`.
- `.complete(callback)`: resolves when everything is written; rejects with an `AggregateError` (`err.failures`, `err.report`) on any failed page, controller, callback, Sass file, pipeline step or redirects write. A chain without it exits 0 on a broken build.
- `.report()`: the last settled build as data (`ok`, `pages`, `failures`, `assets`, `links`, `redirects`, `audit`, `thirdParty` and more). GUIDE.md § Checking a build has the shape.
- `.sitemap(options, callback)`, `.llms(options, callback)`, `.feed(options, callback)`, `.robots(options, callback)`: `sitemap.xml`, the llmstxt.org index, RSS and `robots.txt`, all from one page registry, so every page URL is the page's `{{canonical}}` (`llms.txt` links each page's `.md` copy instead). They need `config.siteUrl`; `.llms()` needs `title` and `summary`; `.feed()` lists pages with a `date`. GUIDE.md § .sitemap(), § .llms(), § .feed(), § .robots().
- Learning packages: pages with `package: '<slug>'` zip into an IMS content package or SCORM 1.2 (`config.packages`). Give each an `id`: the LMS keeps learners' records by it. GUIDE.md § Learning packages; `examples/13-course-packages`.
- Cookie consent: declare every service that stores anything in `config.consent`, and gate it with the consent helpers below. Trap: a gated script never sees `DOMContentLoaded`; site code that loads a third party itself waits with `window.kissConsent.when(name, fn)`. The build writes `kiss-consent.<hash>.js` (the cached client, which the inline part loads), and with an `endpoint` `consent-banners.json`. GUIDE.md § Cookie consent; `examples/14-consent`.
- Markdown copies (`config.markdownCopies`, written when the build calls `.llms()`): every HTML page gets `page.md` (`index.md` for a directory index) beside it, converted from its written `<main>`, and the report names it as `pages[].markdown`. GUIDE.md § Markdown copies for agents.
- `.watch(options)` / `.close()`: dev server and live reload (`dev: true`). A partial edit re-renders the pages that used it; anything else replays the build. Edits to the build script, or to a module a helper entry imports, need a restart.
- `.copyAssets(src, target)`, `.registerPartials()`, `.viewStats()`, `.getModelByID(id, data)`: GUIDE.md § Assets, § Other methods.
- `kiss.handlebars` and `kiss.remarkable`: this instance's own environments. Partials are `.hbs`, `.md` (Markdown first, so `"` args and `{{>` break it), `.html` (compiled, so `{{ }}` interpolates) and `.txt` (escaped, never compiled).
- Named exports: `utils`, the redirect and cache-header encoders (`renderRedirects`, `renderHeadersBlock`, …) and `splitDocument`/`parseHtml`/`findTag` for converting a single-file page (GUIDE.md § Converting an existing page). Deep imports into `kiss-ssg/lib/…` fail by design.
- Types ship in `types/`: `// @ts-check` plus `/** @type {import('kiss-ssg').KissConfigInput} */` gives a plain-JS site full checking.

## Config

Passed to `new Kiss(config)`. Nested blocks merge one level deep; `undefined` takes the default and `null` switches a folder off. Defaults:

```js
{
  dev: false,
  verbose: false,
  cleanBuild: true,     // true empties folders.build first | false | 'atomic'
  extensionLess: false, // true: <path>/<slug>/index.html
  siteUrl: undefined,   // needed by sitemap, llms, feed, robots, canonical, absUrl
  sass: { includePaths: [] },
  fetch: { headers: {}, timeout: 10000, retries: 0, cache: false },
  assets: { hash: false, version: null, minify: true, purge: null, pipeline: [] }, // purge: { files, safelist }
  markdown: { html: true, xhtmlOut: true, breaks: false },
  links: { check: true, canonical: false, trailingSlash: true, hostServed: [] },
  host: null, // 'netlify' | 'cloudflare' | 'firebase' | 'vercel' | 'github-pages' | a list
  redirects: { format: null }, // null: follows host
  cacheHeaders: { format: null }, // null: follows host
  audit: { check: true, ignore: [], privacyPage: null },
  markdownCopies: { write: 'llms', selector: 'main' }, // true: always; false: never
  packages: { format: 'imscp', dir: 'packages', title: null, only: null, schemas: false }, // zips for pages with `package`; false: none
  consent: null, // { services: { gtm: { id } } } turns on the cookie consent manager
  port: 3001,
  livereloadPort: 35729,
  devHost: '127.0.0.1',
  folders: {
    src: './src',       // setting src re-derives the next six
    pages: './src/pages',
    build: './public',
    assets: './src/assets',
    layouts: './src/layouts',
    partials: './src/partials',
    models: './src/models',
    controllers: './src/controllers',
    aikb: './AIKB',
    helpers: './helpers',
  },
}
```

Each key's prose is in GUIDE.md: § Cleaning the build folder, § Building more than one site from one source tree, § Remote models, § Assets, § Markdown options, § Host URL policy, § Redirects, § Cache headers, § Checking a build.

## Traps nothing reports

- `cleanBuild: true` empties the build folder **before** anything renders, so a failed build leaves it empty. Use `'atomic'` for published output. A `dev` run writes a dev build into `folders.build`, so point dev at a git-ignored folder if that folder is published.
- `links.trailingSlash` and `host` are statements about your host, not defaults kiss can get right: Netlify serves `/courses/`, Firebase with `trailingSlash: false` serves `/courses`, and no host file is written until `host` (or a `format`) names one. kiss marks only hashed files `immutable`; never give an unhashed one a year.
- `{{asset}}` renders **no leading slash**: write `href="/{{asset "css/site.css"}}"`. `{{root}}` is a value your page supplies, not a helper.
- `{{#isActive this href="/about"}}{{active}}{{/isActive}}`: the positional argument is the page context (`this`, or `..` in an `{{#each}}`), and the block **always** renders, so the match is `{{active}}`.
- A pipeline step writes into your assets folder, so the copy claims and hashes it. One that can only write into the build folder lists those files in its `outputs` (`['img/icons.svg']`): kiss deletes them first, checks them after, claims them for `{{asset}}` and packages, and never hashes them.
- Tailwind in `assets.pipeline`: keep `-i` (without it the CLI exits 0 and drops everything you authored), and use `@import 'tailwindcss' source(none)` plus explicit `@source` paths, or words in your docs change the hashed stylesheet name on every page. `examples/10-asset-pipeline`.
- A layout with no `<main>` around the page's own content puts its header, footer and menus (any not in a `<nav>`) into every page's `.md` copy. Wrap the content in `<main>`, or set `markdownCopies.selector`.
- `<lastmod>` is a page's `sitemapLastmod`, `updated` or `date`, else omitted. Change the date with the content, never on a rebuild.

## Helpers

GUIDE.md § Helpers has the full rules. Layouts come from `handlebars-layouts`: a layout declares `{{#block "body"}}…{{/block}}`, and a page fills it with `{{#extend "layout"}}{{#content "body"}}…{{/content}}{{/extend}}` (`mode="append"` adds to a slot).

- `markdown`: block or value, rendered through `kiss.remarkable`.
- `sass`: a file path (resolved against `process.cwd()`) and/or an inline block.
- `offset`: `index + 1`.
- `stringify`: `{{{stringify this}}}` to inspect scope.
- `lookup`: the built-in, plus a warning naming an undefined key.
- `isActive`: see the trap above. `folderMatch=true` matches descendants; `{{@current}}`: the page itself.
- `canonical`: the page's absolute URL, the same string as its `<loc>`.
- `absUrl`: `siteUrl` joined to a path, extension kept.
- `asset`: the emitted path under `config.assets` (hash or `?v=`); fails the build on a file not emitted.
- `link`: a page's served path by `id` (`{{link "blog/post" slug=post.slug}}`, `absolute=true`, `canonical=true`); fails the build on an unclaimed id. On a package page: relative to it (`relative=`).
- `env`: `{{#env is="dev"}}…{{else}}…{{/env}}`.
- `scormBridge`: in `<head>`, gives a package page `window.kissScorm`. Trap: the page reports its own completion (`kissScorm.status('completed')`); `complete="seen"` on a bookmarking page makes Moodle reopen it in review mode, saving nothing.
- `embed`: a click-to-load player, map or post (youtube, vimeo, google-maps, instagram, soundcloud), any site; `title=` required.
- `consentHead`: in `<head>` after `<meta charset>`, before any script; needs `config.consent`.
- `consentBanner`: first in `<body>`; the default banner, or the site's `consent-banner` partial.
- `consentScript`: a service's scripts, held back until allowed (`{{consentScript "gtm" id=…}}`, or a block).
- `consentSettings`: the "Cookie settings" control, for every footer.
- `consentTable`: the cookie declaration, for the cookie page.
- `consentRecord`: the visitor's own consent history, from the browser's log, for the privacy page; `ui.history: '<its page id>'` links it from the settings dialog.

Your own helpers: `helpers/index.js` exports `registerHelpers(kiss)`, called with the instance; read config at render time from `options.data.root.config`. GUIDE.md § Helpers has a JSON-LD recipe that escapes `</script>`.

## Checking a build

`npx kiss-ssg check <script> [args…]` runs the build staged and discarded, prints one JSON report per `Kiss` instance (`--summary`: one line each), and exits 1 on any failure. Links, redirects and the launch-readiness audit are advisory and never change the exit code; build the audit's checks in rather than meeting them as findings. `npx kiss-ssg aikb <script>` is the same run, and records `AIKB/` when it passes. GUIDE.md § Checking a build (the report, the audit, `KISS_*` variables), § Recording the knowledge base; the `kiss-build-check` skill reads the report. `session` and `base` answer the kiss-memory skills' git questions: call them, never shell. `speed <build-folder>` gives Lighthouse KPIs (after `npm install -D lighthouse`), `css <build-folder>` audits where CSS goes: GUIDE.md § Measuring speed, § Auditing CSS.

`npx kiss-ssg@latest upgrade` installs that release into the site, checks it landed (not a link, and pinned in package.json and the lockfile), and prints the `CHANGELOG.md` upgrade notes since the site's version. Trap: run it by version; a site's own older bin has no `upgrade`. GUIDE.md § Upgrading a site; the `kiss-site-migrate` skill.
